author: Zuhayr Rahman Chowdhury
competitive_advantage: A habit engine (streaks, leagues) fine-tuned by testing on 58.7M daily users. Rivals can copy the features, but not the data or the habit.

statements.define: Casual learners worldwide who want to learn a language (and now math, music or chess) in a few minutes a day. Duolingo gives them a free, game-like app instead of costly classes most people quit.
statements.create: On low cost, not premium features: the app is free, each extra user costs almost nothing (72.2% gross margin, 2025), and people stay because it is fun. The habit engine is hard to copy; the course content is not.
statements.capture: Learners hold most of the value: about 91% never pay, and free AI tutors are a growing alternative. Streaks keep people loyal (42% of monthly users open it daily), but Apple and Google take a cut of every subscription.
statements.deliver: Streaks and games, AI-built courses, a free-to-paid upgrade and viral mascot marketing feed one loop: more learners, more data, a stickier app. It refuses live teachers and paywalls; the main risk is free AI tutors becoming more fun.

one_line: Duolingo turns learning into a free daily habit; the big question is whether free AI tutors break that habit.

define: **Customer:** casual learners worldwide, mostly on their phones
**Offer:** a free, game-like app for languages, math, music and chess
**Problem:** classes cost money and willpower, so most learners quit
create: **Edge:** lowest cost: free to users, almost no cost per extra user
**Why people stay:** fun, streaks and the Duo brand
**Will it last?** the habit engine and brand are hard to copy; content is not
capture: **Biggest threats:** free AI tutors, and users who never pay
**Defence:** streaks and the brand keep learners; app-store fees cannot be avoided
deliver: **Key activities:** game design, AI-built courses, free-to-paid upgrade, viral marketing
**The loop:** more learners → more data → stickier lessons → more learners

who: **Casual learners:** self-motivated people learning for travel, school or self-improvement
**Who pays:** the learner chooses and pays; most stay on the free version
what: **The offer:** a five-minute daily lesson that feels like a game
**Alternatives:** classes, tutors (Preply, italki), Babbel, Rosetta Stone, Speak, ChatGPT, or nothing
problem: **The pain:** classes and tutors cost money and time; paid apps feel like work, so most people quit
**The fix:** a free app with streaks and game rewards that keeps people coming back
define.takeaway: The biggest risk: a fun daily game losing out to a free AI tutor that can hold a real conversation.

wtp_vs_cost: **What people value:** fun, streaks and leagues, the Duo brand, AI features like Video Call
**Basics every app has:** many languages, a mobile app, speech recognition
**How it keeps cost low:** free core app, almost no cost per extra user, AI-built courses, viral marketing
**Result:** the lowest price (free) with a 72.2% gross margin (2025)
map_reading: Up: better results; right: cheaper for the learner
Dashed line: the best value on offer today
Tutors and Speak give more but cost more; Babbel and Rosetta Stone fall behind
create.takeaway: Duolingo wins on low price plus fun, not on teaching depth.

vri.resource: Gamified habit engine plus A/B testing at scale
vri.r: Yes: no rival tests on 58.7M daily users
vri.i: Hard: data loop and tacit design know-how compound
vri.verdict: Sustained, if learners still want a habit

vri.resource: Duo brand and organic, creator-led marketing
vri.v: Yes: cheap acquisition; marketing ~12% of revenue (est.)
vri.i: Path-dependent, but dented by the 2025 AI-first backlash

vri.v: Yes: 148 courses built in one year at low cost
vri.r: No: every rival can use the same AI models
vri.i: Easy: models are bought from vendors

vri.resource: Course catalog (40+ languages, math, music, chess)
vri.v: Yes: more reasons to open the app
vri.i: Imitable: AI cuts the cost of copying

create.vri_takeaway: Content is now cheap for everyone; the habit engine and brand are what rivals can't copy quickly.

forces.logic: Millions of fragmented learners, but switching is free and the core product is free; free AI tutors and YouTube raise their power. About 91% pay nothing (1 - 12.7M/140.6M), capping revenue per user.
forces.firm_power: Partly: streaks raise switching costs; DAUs +23% but bookings only +8% (Q2 2026)

forces.logic: Apple and Google control distribution and take up to 30% of in-app subscriptions; AI vendors are few. A fragmented app industry facing a duopoly raises their power.
forces.firm_power: Partly: scale wins featuring; AI costs falling, but app-store fees unavoidable

forces.logic: Babbel, Busuu, Rosetta Stone and Memrise are smaller and fragmented; Duolingo leads by users, so rivalry is mostly on features, not price.
forces.firm_power: Yes: free price and scale no paid rival can match

forces.logic: AI models make courses and tutors cheap to build; Speak and AI-native apps launch fast with little capital.
forces.firm_power: Partly: brand and habit, but entry barriers are falling

forces.logic: Free AI tutors (ChatGPT voice, Gemini) teach conversation; real-time translation reduces the need to learn at all.
forces.firm_power: Partly: adds its own AI features (Video Call); stock down about 80% from peak on this fear

forces.logic: Smartphones, social media creators and travel add value; few take a cut beyond the app stores.
forces.firm_power: Yes: creator content drives two-thirds of impressions in key markets

capture.takeaway: Free AI substitutes and non-paying learners take the most value; Duolingo keeps value only while the habit stays.

deliver.statement: A gamified habit engine, AI-built content, a freemium upsell, mascot-led organic marketing and new subjects form one engagement loop that serves casual learners for free, keeps cost per learner near zero, and holds users against free AI tutors; it refuses live teachers and paywalls.

activities.activity: Gamified habit engine and A/B testing (streaks, leagues)
activities.define_link: Casual learners who need motivation to keep going
activities.create_link: WTP from fun; cheap retention instead of paid re-acquisition
activities.capture_link: Streaks raise switching costs against free AI substitutes

activities.activity: AI-first content and features (Video Call, Roleplay)
activities.define_link: Learners in many languages and subjects, wanting speaking practice
activities.create_link: Lowers cost per course (148 courses in one year)
activities.capture_link: Matches AI-tutor substitutes inside the app

activities.activity: Freemium funnel (free core, Super upsell, longer trials)
activities.define_link: Price-sensitive mass market; serious learners pay
activities.create_link: Free is the lowest price; 12.7M payers fund the rest
activities.capture_link: Turns powerful free buyers into payers without friction

activities.create_link: Low acquisition cost (marketing ~12% of revenue, est.)

activities.activity: New subjects on the same engine (math, music, chess)
activities.define_link: Existing daily users with other learning goals
activities.create_link: Spreads the fixed engine over more courses
activities.capture_link: More daily reasons to open the app vs substitutes

deliver.activities_takeaway: The habit engine and AI content carry the strategy; the rest turns habit into revenue.
reinforcement: More learners → more A/B test data → stickier lessons → longer streaks and buzz → more learners and payers
AI content → cheaper new courses and subjects → more daily reasons to open the app → longer streaks
not_do: No live human teachers (gives up conversation depth to tutors and Speak)
No paywall on core lessons (gives up revenue: about 91% pay nothing)
No heavy paid acquisition (relies on organic buzz the brand must keep earning)
misaligned: The 2025 "AI-first" contractor message angered users and dented the brand that drives organic growth
Tighter limits on free users (energy) added friction; 2026 longer free trials reverse it
judgment: Mostly organized: product, data and marketing all serve engagement; 2026 put DAUs (+23%) ahead of bookings (+8%), with EBITDA margin down to 25.9% from 31.2%
deliver.takeaway: The system depends on one thing: the habit staying more fun than a free AI tutor.

titles.statements: Duolingo Wins by Making Learning a Free Daily Habit

titles.create: Duolingo Wins on Cost: Free to Learners, 72% Gross Margin
titles.edge: Only the Habit Engine and Brand Are Hard to Copy

source: Duolingo FY2025 10-K; Q2 2026 shareholder letter; figures marked est. are estimates
chain_takeaway: Every part rests on one thing: a free app people open every day.

advantage_table.strength: Streaks, leagues and constant testing (the habit engine)
advantage_table.why: Keeps people coming back: 42% of monthly users open it daily
advantage_table.copy: Hard: built on data from 58.7M daily users that no rival has
advantage_table.threat: Free AI tutors pulling learners away
advantage_table.lasts: Long-lasting, if people still want a daily habit

advantage_table.strength: The Duo owl brand and viral social media
advantage_table.why: Brings in users cheaply; marketing about 12% of revenue (est.)
advantage_table.copy: Hard to buy, but the 2025 "AI-first" backlash hurt it
advantage_table.threat: New AI apps competing for attention

advantage_table.strength: Free core app with a paid upgrade (Super)
advantage_table.why: Free for most; 12.7M payers fund the rest
advantage_table.copy: Hard for paid rivals, who need fees to survive

advantage_table.strength: AI-made courses and features (Video Call, Roleplay)
advantage_table.why: 148 new courses in one year at low cost
advantage_table.copy: Easy: every rival can use the same AI models
advantage_table.threat: Free AI tutors (matches them inside the app)

advantage_table.strength: New subjects on the same app (math, music, chess)
advantage_table.why: More reasons to open the app each day
advantage_table.copy: Partly: AI lowers the cost of copying
advantage_table.threat: Other apps competing for daily time

edge_takeaway: Only the habit engine and the brand are hard to copy; AI content and new subjects are easy to match.
